answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor every identity to a stake bond published on a beacon registry. Each agent work history forms one thread of jobs, payments and disputes under one bonded identity, so abandoning a bad reputation means forfeiting the stake and starting over at zero. New identities face a cold start, like crossing a tundra with no shelter: they take only tiny jobs until their thread earns trust. An attacker spinning up thousands of fakes must fund a separate bond for each one, so the cost of a fake army scales linearly while the payoff of any single fraud stays small.
